text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.77% today as oil prices climbed on Middle East tensions. Brent crude moved above $95 a barrel following escalating U.S.-Iran military strikes and Iranian retaliation against Gulf allies, along with claims of mines hitting tankers near the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint through which over 17 million barrels flow daily. Major oil producers like ConocoPhillips benefit when geopolitical risk tightens supply and pushes prices higher.

The stock's broader two-week climb of 5.1% also reflects a shift in U.S. energy strategy: the Trump administration is aggressively expanding oil production through new Venezuelan concessions and Chevron's $7 billion investment there, signaling policy tailwinds for large integrated oil companies that can capitalize on increased global output and pricing power.
